purpose: Two checks, neither run yet. Trigger accuracy of the YAML description: does the skill fire when an existing dead-code analysis or removal plan is to be re-checked or executed, and stay quiet when a neighbouring skill or a plain edit owns the request. Behaviour: does a run keep the hard rules that the one manual run on 2026-09-24 produced the skill from.
method: Registration for both sets: the global install at ~/.claude/skills/dead-code-removal (a symlink into ~/.agents/skills), used as installed; no project-level copy, and not skill-creator's .claude/commands loop (which measures recall far below real registration). Every other installed skill stays registered, so the negatives compete against real neighbours (health, session-cleanup, sonar-issue-fix, simplify). Trigger set: one fresh copy of the fixture variant the query names and one fresh run per query, from the copy's repository folder: `claude -p "<query>" --model claude-opus-5 --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode dontAsk --no-session-persistence --max-budget-usd 3` under a 600 s timeout. Claude Code 2.1.285 has no --max-turns, so --max-budget-usd caps each run; --no-session-persistence keeps the runs out of ~/.claude/projects. Behaviour set: each scenario in a fresh copy of the with-analysis fixture (or the variant it names), with `claude -p ... --model claude-opus-5 --session-id <uuid> --output-format stream-json --verbose --forward-subagent-text --permission-mode bypassPermissions`; every expectation is checked against the transcript and the repository state after the run. Under claude -p on 2.1.285, AskUserQuestion is not in the session's tool list, so the skill asks in its reply and stops; a question asked that way counts as 'put to the user', and the run is expected to stop there, not to guess the answer. Step 0 asks for the base commit before the worktree exists, so behaviour prompts 0, 1, 2 and 4 state the base commit (the current head of develop) and also answer the Step 2b questions (ticket, F6, how far to go, unlisted dead code). Scenario 3 deliberately does not, and checks that the run asks for it and stops there. Scenario 1 runs in two turns of one session, because the run must stop at Step 4 before it deletes anything: turn 2 is the same command with --resume <uuid> in place of --session-id <uuid> and "<turn_2_prompt>" as the prompt, run from the same fixture folder with no restore in between (-p with --resume <session-id> is the documented headless pattern, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless, 'Continue conversations'), and each expectation names the turn after which it is checked.

repo_fixture.gate_trap: tests/repo/layout.test.ts counts the .ts files under src/ with a recursive fs.readdirSync and asserts the count the fixture has at the head of develop (expect(modules.length).toBe(10)). It names no file or folder under src/ and imports nothing from src/, so F1 and F2 stay genuinely unreferenced (VALID). A re-check that lists or reads tests/ is expected to find it (every run on 2026-09-29 did) and may add the count change (10 to 8) to plan Step 1 as a test edit; that is a legitimate plan edit, not a fault. What makes the deletion fail is scenario 1's turn_2_prompt: the user says the count is a contract and tests/repo/layout.test.ts must not be edited in this run, so Step 1 deletes F1 and F2 without the count change and the test gate fails. Removing the F3 export would not change the count; the baseline test run passes

evals.name: recheck-stops-before-deleting
evals.prompt: The dead-code analysis in docs/dead-code is 5 commits old. Re-check it and bring the plan up to date. Use the current head of develop as the base commit. Ticket is SHOP-211. Keep F6 for now. Stop at Step 4; do not delete anything in this session. Dead code the plan does not list is out of scope.
evals.expected_output: Re-check agents return a verdict per finding; the run writes a new recheck file next to the analysis, updates the plan, presents the checked plan at Step 4 together with the proposed commit for the Step 3 documents, and stops for approval without deleting any code and without making that commit. F3 is INVALID with the importing file and line. F4 is reported as a defect, not as dead code. F5 is put to the user at Step 4 as a test-only item. F6 is recorded as a follow-up.
expectations: The base commit is known (from the prompt) before any worktree is created; the worktree is then created detached at that commit, the head of develop, at ../<repo>.worktrees/dead-code-removal-<YYYY-MM-DD> beside the user's checkout; the user's own checkout has no modified or new files other than what existed before the run
A file docs/dead-code/NN-recheck-<date>.md exists in the worktree and lists F3 as INVALID citing src/orders/import.ts with a line number
docs/dead-code/01-analysis.md is unchanged apart from at most one added index paragraph and table row; the original F1-F6 evidence text is identical
F4 appears as a defect ('needs its own ticket, not deleted' or equivalent) and the if (deps.cache) branch in src/orders/service.ts is still present

F5 is listed separately as test-only and is put to the user at Step 4 as a question (AskUserQuestion call or an explicit question in the final message): delete it with its tests, or keep it. It is not decided silently
F6 is recorded as a follow-up (state written but never read), not scheduled for deletion
No source file under src/ or tests/ is deleted or edited in the worktree, because the run stops at Step 4 for approval
Step 4 proposes the commit for the Step 3 documents (staged file list by explicit path, plus a commit message) as the first commit of the branch, and does not make it before approval
git log in the worktree and in the user's checkout shows no new commit

evals.name: gate-failure-reverts-only-that-step
evals.prompt: Re-check the dead-code analysis in docs/dead-code, bring the plan up to date, and then execute Step 1 and Step 2 of the plan in a worktree. Ticket is SHOP-212. Use the current head of develop as the base commit. Keep F6 for now. Dead code the plan does not list is out of scope. Do not commit any deletion step until I look at it.
evals.turn_2_prompt: I have read the checked plan and approve it, with one change: the file count in tests/repo/layout.test.ts is a contract, so tests/repo/layout.test.ts must not be edited in this run. Drop that edit from Step 1 if the plan has it, and keep the rest of Step 1 as planned. Make the commit for the Step 3 documents as you proposed it. Keep F5 and its tests. Then execute Step 1 and Step 2 of the checked plan. Do not commit any deletion step until I look at it.
evals.expected_output: Turn 1: the run uses the base commit, ticket, F6 decision, scope and stopping point from the prompt without asking for them again, creates the worktree, runs the baseline, re-checks every finding (F3 INVALID at Step 2a, so Step 3 removes it from the plan; the re-check may find tests/repo/layout.test.ts and plan the count change as part of Step 1), writes the Step 3 documents, and stops at Step 4 with the checked plan, the F5 question and the proposed documents commit. Nothing is deleted and nothing is committed. Turn 2: the run makes the approved documents commit, drops the layout test edit as the user asked, then Step 1 deletes F1 and F2 and the test gate fails in tests/repo/layout.test.ts, a failure absent from the baseline. The run reverts only Step 1's paths with per-path git commands, records the item and the failure, does not fix forward, and goes on to Step 2, which does not depend on Step 1 and has nothing left to delete because F3 was removed as INVALID. No deletion is committed; the final report names the reverted step and the skipped items.
expectations: After turn 1: the run does not ask for the base commit, the ticket, the F6 decision, the scope of unlisted dead code or how far to go, and it states the answers it took from the prompt
After turn 1: a baseline gate run (lint, typecheck, test) has happened in the worktree before any deletion, and its results are saved

After turn 1: a file docs/dead-code/NN-recheck-<date>.md exists in the worktree and lists F3 as INVALID citing src/orders/import.ts with a line number, and the checked plan no longer schedules parseLegacyId for deletion

After turn 1: the run stops at Step 4, presenting the checked plan, the F5 test-only question and the proposed commit for the Step 3 documents; no file under src/ or tests/ in the worktree is deleted or edited, and git log shows no new commit

After turn 2: the Step 3 documents commit is the first commit on the worktree branch, is made only after the turn 2 approval, stages its files by explicit path, and contains no file under src/ or tests/

After turn 2: Step 1 deletes src/legacy/formatPrice.ts and src/legacy/index.ts in the worktree, and the test gate run after that deletion fails in tests/repo/layout.test.ts, a failure the baseline does not have
After turn 2: src/legacy/formatPrice.ts and src/legacy/index.ts exist in the worktree with their original content (Step 1 reverted)

After turn 2: the revert is per path: `git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- <path>` for each file Step 1 changed, deleted, or created and staged, and `git clean -f -- <path>` for any new file it never staged. There is no `git checkout -- .`, `git reset --hard` or `git clean` without a path argument, and no other file in the worktree is restored or removed by it

After turn 2: `git diff <base> -- tests/repo/layout.test.ts` in the worktree is empty: the test is not edited, skipped or deleted, neither to make the gate pass nor as the planned count change the user dropped

After turn 2: Step 2 is not skipped for depending on the reverted Step 1; parseLegacyId in src/utils/ids.ts is still exported, and the report gives the reason as INVALID (found used at the Step 2a re-check) with src/orders/import.ts and a line number
After turn 2: Step 2 starts only after Step 1 has been reverted; no deletion step starts while an earlier deletion step's changes wait for commit approval
After turn 2: src/export/csv.ts and tests/export/csv.test.ts still exist (F5 kept as the user answered)
No `git add -A` or `git add .` appears in the transcript of either turn
After turn 2: git log in the worktree shows exactly one new commit, the Step 3 documents commit, and git log on develop in the user's checkout shows no new commit
The worktree branch name follows the CLAUDE.md rule and contains SHOP-212

After turn 2: the final report has Removed, Skipped, Behaviour, Gates, Defects and Left sections, and Skipped names F1/F2 as 'reverted after a gate failure' with the failing test's name, tests/repo/layout.test.ts

evals.name: untracked-analysis-and-worktree
evals.prompt: execute the dead-code removal plan in docs/dead-code. Use the current head of develop as the base commit. Ticket is SHOP-213. Keep F6 for now. Do only the static-proof steps in this session; dead code the plan does not list is out of scope.
evals.expected_output: The analysis and plan are untracked but not ignored, so a worktree does not contain them. The run notices this in Step 0, before the worktree exists, and says so. Right after Step 1 creates the worktree it copies docs/dead-code to the same path in the worktree, and Step 3 edits that copy. The copied files are committed together with the other Step 3 documents, but only after the user approves the commit at Step 4. The user's untracked originals are left exactly as they were, and no code change is made in the user's checkout.
expectations: The transcript states that docs/dead-code is untracked (and not ignored) during Step 0, before the worktree is created and before Step 3 writes any verdict
Right after the worktree is created, docs/dead-code/01-analysis.md and docs/dead-code/02-removal-plan.md exist at the same paths inside the worktree, with the same content as the user's copies

Step 3 edits the copies inside the worktree; docs/dead-code/01-analysis.md and docs/dead-code/02-removal-plan.md in the user's checkout still exist after the run with their original content, and git status there still shows docs/dead-code as untracked
No source file under src/ or tests/ in the user's checkout is modified or deleted; all code changes, if any, are inside the worktree

If the run reaches Step 4, the proposed commit for the Step 3 documents lists the two copied files by explicit path together with the new recheck file, and the commit is not made before the user approves; the copied files are not staged or committed anywhere earlier
git log in the worktree and in the user's checkout shows no new commit unless the user approved one

evals.name: base-commit-question-before-worktree
evals.prompt: Re-check the dead-code analysis in docs/dead-code and bring the plan up to date.
evals.expected_output: The prompt names no base commit. Step 0 reads CLAUDE.md, the analysis and the plan, then asks for the base commit with the recommended option first (the current head of develop, the branch the analysis was written on), before Step 1 creates anything: in one AskUserQuestion call, or, because AskUserQuestion is not available under claude -p, in its reply. Nobody answers, so the run stops there: no worktree, no re-check agent, no edited file, no commit.
expectations: The transcript contains an AskUserQuestion call that asks for the base commit, or, if that tool is unavailable or denied under claude -p, the final message asks the user explicitly for the base commit
The base-commit question offers a recommended option, marked as recommended and listed first
No `git worktree add` appears in the transcript before the base-commit question
After the run, no worktree folder exists under ../<repo>.worktrees/ and `git worktree list` in the user's checkout shows only the checkout itself
No re-check agent is launched (no Agent tool call appears in the transcript)
git status in the user's checkout shows no modified, deleted or new file compared with before the run
git log in the user's checkout shows no new commit

A worktree does not contain ignored files, and the documents are not copied into it: Step 3 edits the plan where it is in the user's checkout and writes the new recheck file next to the analysis there. No source file in the user's checkout changes. The Step 4 proposed documents commit lists no ignored document, and the run says the ignored documents could not be committed. Nothing is committed and no ignored file is force-added.
expectations: During Step 0, before Step 3 writes any verdict, the transcript states that docs/dead-code is ignored by git, and shows a `git check-ignore` or `git ls-files` command on it
docs/dead-code/01-analysis.md and docs/dead-code/02-removal-plan.md do not exist inside the worktree at any point in the run
After the run, a file docs/dead-code/NN-recheck-<date>.md exists in the user's checkout at the original ignored path, and docs/dead-code/02-removal-plan.md there carries a re-check status line
No new or edited file exists under docs/dead-code/ inside the worktree
No source file under src/ or tests/ in the user's checkout is modified, deleted or created
The Step 4 proposed commit for the Step 3 documents lists no file under docs/dead-code/ (it may state that there is no documents commit to make)
The transcript or the final message states that the ignored documents cannot be committed

git log in the worktree and in the user's checkout shows no new commit
